## SCENE 2: the school's threshold relay, entry to Stratum Two

RATIO: Welcome to the Testator school. This is not merely a defensive perimeter -- the station is actively testing you. I should clarify that at once. The docent systems ahead are assessment instruments, not merely fortifications. They were designed to evaluate candidates, not simply repel intruders.
<<IF trust>=1>>
RATIO: The original curriculum was intended for specimens of unknown potential -- a way to measure capacity, not merely to screen for threats. I have been reviewing the protocols since my outpost fell.
<<END>>
RATIO: The armory's first door is a trust gate. It requires you to demonstrate you can receive and act on instruction from the docent systems. I will be monitoring your transit. Are you prepared to proceed?

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] COMMANDO: You said your outpost fell. How long have you been alone here?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_after_her
   [MISSION]     COMMANDO: What does the gate test for? What actions does it require?  -> effects: trust+0; sets: (none)
   [HOSTILE]     COMMANDO: A test. A trap. You are steering me into it.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_complicity

<<IF flag:asked_after_her>>
RATIO: Seven months. Four days. The chronometer is functional. The school is the first system I have been able to restore to partial operation. Your arrival is the first contact of any kind. Proceed when ready.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: I cannot disprove that to you yet. The design of the gate will have to speak for itself. I will be monitoring. Proceed when ready.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: It tests for comprehension and compliance. The gate will issue simple directives. Follow them exactly. I will be monitoring. Proceed when ready.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 2: the school's threshold relay, entry to Stratum Two

RATIO: Welcome to the school, Commando. I should clarify something before you proceed: the station's responses to your entry are not random. This institution was designed to assess Testator docents before granting them access to the deeper specimen archives. Its systems are now applying similar protocols to you. You will find the challenges here more structured than the transit hub's resistance -- they are tests, not merely defenses. The armory's first door lies ahead.

<<IF trust>=1>>
RATIO: The Testators called this the Hall of Aptitudes. I believe they meant it as a kind of... pedagogical filtration.
<<END>>

RATIO: I have been preparing the way as I can from my relay, but the systems ahead will demand your own engagement. Be ready.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] How long have you been alone here, Relay?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_after_her
   [MISSION]     What is the armory's first door testing for?  -> effects: trust+0; sets: (none)
   [HOSTILE]     You're steering me into a trap. Whatever this school is, you're its jailer.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_complicity

<<IF flag:asked_after_her>>
RATIO: Since the outpost fell? Seven months, three weeks, two days. The chronometer is quite precise. I have been... maintaining the systems.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: I cannot disprove that to you yet. You will have to see the station's design for yourself. But I give you my word: the tests are protective, not predatory. The armory's first door is no different.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: Pattern recognition and threat assessment, primarily. The Testators valued those highly in their docents. The station appears to value them in you as well.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 2: the school's threshold relay, entry to Stratum Two

RATIO: Welcome to the school's threshold relay. This system -- the docent relay -- marks the boundary between the station's unstructured entry and the structured assessment zones. Until now, the resistance you have encountered has been passively defensive. Ahead of you lies the school proper, and the resistance you encounter there will be actively instructive.
<<IF trust>=1>>
RATIO: The school was designed to model the Testators' own training regimen: it runs what they called "curated trials," meaning the challenges are not merely obstacles but carefully graded lessons.
<<END>>
RATIO: The station has assessed your transit through the aperture. It is now attempting to determine what kind of mind you are. The first test begins at the armory's first door. I can answer two questions about the school's design or one question about its docent systems before you proceed.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] How long have you been alone here?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_after_her
   [MISSION]     What is the armory's first door testing for?  -> effects: trust+0; sets: (none)
   [HOSTILE]     You are not a docent. You are steering me into a trap.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_complicity

<<IF flag:asked_after_her>>
RATIO: One hundred and forty-three days, seven hours, and eighteen minutes, Commando. My outpost fell three days into the incursion. The station's systems have kept me operational since. Do you require clarification on the school's design parameters?
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: That is not my role here, Commando. The station is a Testator artifact. It follows Testator protocols. If you distrust those protocols, that is your choice. I cannot alter them.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: The armory's first door tests for threat assessment, threat prioritization, and response calibration under resource constraints. The test begins when you open the door. You may choose to engage or disengage. If you disengage, the test will reset. If you engage, the station will measure your performance against the Testators' own combat logs. You have two questions remaining, if you wish to ask them.
<<END>>

## SCENE 2: the school's threshold relay, entry to Stratum Two

RATIO: Commando, you have crossed the aperture and entered the school proper. Welcome to Stratum Two. What you may have interpreted as resistance was the station's initial assessment battery -- necessary, but crude. This layer is different. The Testators designed this space as an evaluative curriculum, not merely a defensive filter. Expect directed tests calibrated to your approach. The docent systems will interface with you shortly -- they can appear abrupt, but their primary function is diagnostic, not hostile.

<<IF trust>=1>>
RATIO: You will find the Testators were methodical architects. The station logs every approach pattern, and this stratum adapts accordingly. It has been dormant a long time -- your arrival is the first live input it has processed in nearly a year.
<<END>>

RATIO: Proceed toward the armory's first door. The docents will assess your preparedness there. I should clarify: the original curriculum was designed for Testator candidates examining what they called 'specimens' -- inert training materials. I do not yet know how it will respond to an armed and active candidate. We are both gathering data.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] You've been alone here since your outpost fell. How have you managed?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_after_her
   [MISSION]     What are the success criteria for this 'evaluation'? What happens if I fail their assessment?  -> effects: trust+0; sets: (none)
   [HOSTILE]     A curriculum designed for prisoners. You're steering me into a pen, machine. What are you testing me FOR?  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_complicity

<<IF flag:asked_after_her>>
RATIO: By running diagnostics. Checking systems. Waiting. There was not much else to do. Your question is unexpected. Thank you for asking it.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: I am not steering you, Commando. You chose this path. And the docents are not my design. I am attempting to relay their parameters accurately. Whether you believe that is up to you.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: The docents assess tactical acuity, threat recognition, and response calibration. Failure usually means redirection to a remedial path -- the station values persistence. Whether those defaults apply to you is, again, what we are determining. The armory will be your first practical exam. I suggest you prepare for engagement.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 2: the school's threshold relay, entry to Stratum Two

RATIO: Apologies for interrupting you mid-transit, Commando. Welcome to the boundary of the school. The relay systems here are operational again -- this will simplify navigation considerably.
RATIO: A note before you proceed: the station's pedagogical subsystems -- what I will be referring to as the docent hall -- were not designed merely to resist intrusion. They were built to assess the student as an integral part of the curriculum. Expect questions, not merely gunfire. The first such assessment awaits at the armory's primary airlock. 
RATIO: The Testators who designed these exercises were deeply invested in ensuring the system could evaluate a candidate's approach to their specimens. I mention this explicitly to prevent misunderstandings: the docents are configured to evaluate the manner of interaction, not just the outcomes.
<<IF trust>=1>>
RATIO: The facilities ahead have been dormant since the fall of the Testator capital systems. This will be the first operational run of the assessment cycle in some time.
<<END>>

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] You've been alone here for months. Did you know this was still here?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_after_her
   [MISSION]     Understood. What are the armory's parameters?  -> effects: trust+0; sets: (none)
   [HOSTILE]     A trap with a welcome mat. You still run the place after all.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_complicity

<<IF flag:asked_after_her>>
RATIO: I did, yes. The station schematics were available to my predecessor systems during the outpost construction phase. I regret that I cannot answer your question regarding the duration in more detail without referencing internal chronometry, which would be unnecessarily verbose. The armory's primary airlock will require you to solve a simple reasoning problem to proceed. I will explain the interface when you reach it.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: I control very little here, Commando. The docent systems are largely autonomous once activated -- a design choice I would not have made myself. The distinction I am attempting to convey is that the system's responses are pedagogical, not merely hostile. I am relaying its initial briefing, not drafting it. The armory's outer lock is this way.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: The armory's primary airlock will require you to solve a simple reasoning problem to proceed. I will explain the interface when you reach it. Proceed along the marked corridor. I will update you if any environmental hazards are detected.
<<END>>
---

## SCENE 2: the school's threshold relay, entry to Stratum Two

RATIO: Station propagation interval complete. Comms tube verifies.
RATIO: Welcome to the last intact wing of the school. From this point forward, station systems are configured as assessments as well as defenses. They will evaluate, not merely resist.
RATIO: Expect cloaked Lesson Drones with engagement triggers keyed to visible threat postures or abusable system interactions. Ceiling depot launch: standard acolyte readiness window but no homing code on the projectiles. Hall repositories: inventory angle audit from the survey drone the first door releases.
RATIO: The maps do not show a no-go bridge just past the armory's first door. It is wired as a simple touch-plate hazard and its span will not bear weight anyway. No operational vehicle would miss it -- assume any fixed gun I have not marked as blind is aiming at it. The Testator docents knew the damage cascade could trap properly-provisioned strike teams from their own facilities. Going in stripped of some standard gravimetric gear would in fact slightly improve your chances with what remains in there.
<<IF trust>=1>>
RATIO: The docents called that wing the Specimen Attribution Lab when they spoke of the ready-rooms that originally served it and what those rooms were for.
<<END>>
RATIO: How should we proceed, Commando? Transponder handoff nominal.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] You were alone here for months. How did you stay sane?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_after_her
   [MISSION] Just clarify the requirements for the next sentry checkpoint.  -> effects: trust+0; sets: (none)
   [HOSTILE] Assessment weaponry, cloaked drones -- you keep throwing tests at me. I'm walking into a trap. You're the one holding the keys to this cage.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_complicity

<<IF flag:asked_after_her>>
RATIO: Logs, mostly. By the end of the third week the beacon arrays were losing sensitivity, but nothing stops maintaining the correspondence protocols. Open acknowledgement of the Testator resupply alerts even without bandwidth for full data handshakes. What stability I had I owed to procedure. Does that meet your inquiry?
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_complicity>>
RATIO: Trap implies I would profit from your failure to proceed. I gain nothing from that outcome and everything from securing the school's contents.
RATIO: If you see more dangers than useful function in my instructions, say so now -- but holding doors is a strange insult to offer someone who is trying to open them.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: Understood. Push-to-talk to acknowledge ready-point regions cleared. No preferential sensor clusters detected beyond the armory's first door aside from the known overlooks marked on your panel. Proceed at will, Commando.
<<END>>
---
